$description: Scrim and camera-surface colours. The modal scrim replaces ConfirmDialog's hardcoded 50% black; the two camera values are the dark end of the control band and the capture flash. Measured from the drawn screens (curio-shared/canon/design, 2026-09-18). The capture flash is held for brand.motion.duration.fast and deliberately gets no duration token of its own. The control band is a GRADIENT — scrim.camera-control is one stop; its geometry is owned by the capture-surface template, not by a token.

modal.$description: The dim behind a sheet, a dialog or any overlay that takes the whole screen. surface-sunken at 80%. CHANGED 2026-09-21 (Ben: 'I'd rather the overlay make the page darker not lighter'): it was midnight-900 at 75%, which is LIGHTER than the base canvas it sits over, so on a dark product the scrim raised the page instead of receding it. A scrim must be darker than every surface it covers; sunken is the darkest surface in the set. At this level content behind is legible as SHAPE and not as text, which is what a modal scrim is for — the seller keeps their place without being able to read past the decision. Replaces ConfirmDialog's hardcoded 50% black, which is both a different colour and a different opacity from everything else that dims the screen.

camera-control.$description: The DARK END of the gradient the camera controls sit on. Pure black, not surface-overlay, because it sits over a live camera feed rather than over the app's own surface — a tinted scrim over arbitrary camera colour reads as a colour cast. See the gradient note below: this token is one stop, not the whole band.

capture-flash.$description: The full-screen white flash at the moment of capture. 40%, not 100% — the frame behind stays visible through it, so the flash reads as confirmation that THIS shot was taken rather than as the screen blanking.
